overview: Machrihanish Bay is a long Atlantic-facing beach on the west coast of Kintyre, running about three miles north from Machrihanish village to Westport. From the south end you look out to Gigha, Islay and Jura, and the village is just north of the Mull of Kintyre.

The village has history beyond golf. The links course was laid out by Old Tom Morris, and the painter William McTaggart drew on the beach and views. In 1905 Reginald Fessenden built a radio station here with a 415-foot mast for transatlantic contact; it blew down in a gale in December 1906.

For surfing, Machrihanish is an exposed beach, point and river-mouth break. Islay and Ireland shelter it from a lot of swell, so it needs a clean westerly. When that lines up with an easterly wind, you have miles of sand to choose from, and Westport at the north end is worth checking too.
suits: Beginners in a lesson at Westport
notFor: Guaranteed waves on any Atlantic swell

text: Surf-forecast gives a west swell with an easterly offshore wind as the best combination, and mid tide on the rising tide as the best window. Beach peaks give lefts and rights, and the point and river mouth add variety.

It can work at any time of year, but autumn is the season most people target. Because the beach is so exposed, strong winds can quickly spoil it, and the long empty stretches mean you should surf with someone.

Machrihanish is an exposed beach, point and river-mouth break that likes a west swell with an east offshore, around mid tide on the rise. It can work at any time of year, with spring best, and April has the most clean days.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Intermediates
cards.text: Competent beginners on small days; the point is for experienced surfers.

cards.label: Tide
cards.title: Mid, rising
cards.text: The most-cited window on this beach.

cards.label: Hazards
cards.title: Rips and isolation
cards.text: Strong currents, rocky outcrops and few people about.

practical.label: Parking
practical.title: Machrihanish village
practical.text: Free council car park opposite the Old Post Office on the B843 (PA28 6PZ), 20 spaces.

practical.label: Parking
practical.title: Westport
practical.text: Free council car park on the A83 (PA28 6QD), 70 spaces.

practical.label: Toilets
practical.title: Open 24 hours
practical.text: Argyll and Bute Council lists the Machrihanish toilets as open 24 hours, all year.

practical.label: Air
practical.title: Campbeltown Airport
practical.text: The former RAF Machrihanish airfield beside the village is now Campbeltown Airport.

practical.label: Lifeguards
practical.title: None
practical.text: Call 999 or 112 and ask for the Coastguard in an emergency.

faqs.a: Islay and Ireland block much of the Atlantic swell. It needs a west swell; check Westport too.
Surf-forecast suggests mid tide on the rising tide.
About three miles from Machrihanish village north to Westport.
Argyll and Bute Council lists both the village and Westport car parks as free.
